title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this and the neighbouring pages). pi_{0,3}^ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 - {0,1,infinity}, i.e. the profinite completion of Gamma(2)/{+-1}, the lambda-line of the Legendre family. Adjoining the S_3 symmetries gives a group containing the elliptic elements sigma_infinity (order 4 in SL_2, sigma^2 = -1) and rho (order 6, rho^2 - rho + 1 = 0). tau_infinity is a 'complex conjugation' involution. M^{!~}_{0,3} is a group of 'loop-equation' data u <-> (alpha, beta, f), pairs of elements of pi^_{0,3} satisfying relation (37)=(97). It is an extension of a quotient N^{!~}_{0,3} by pi^_{0,3} (or by C^+_{0,3}). It comes with a homomorphism u -> underline{u} = u_{alpha,beta,f} into M_2(Z^)^* = GL(2,Z^)'. Concretely this is the action on the Tate module of the Legendre elliptic curve. By (98), u_{alpha,beta,f} = mu (t sigma_infinity + u) tau_infinity^{a}.

Page content, case 1 (base point lambda = 1/2). Define M^{!~}_{0,3}(1/2) = {u : [u, sigma_infinity] = 1}, the centralizer of the order-4 elliptic element; (100) says it maps isomorphically onto N^{!~}_{0,3}. Inverting gives a section-like homomorphism kappa_{1/2} : N^{!~}_{0,3} ≅ M(1/2) ⊂ M^{!~}_{0,3} -> GL(2,Z^). By (98)-(99) its image normalizes the commutative subalgebra Z^[sigma_infinity] ≅ Z^[i] of M_2(Z^). The relation (99) tau sigma tau^{-1} = -sigma = sigma^{-1} is the action of Gal(Q(i)/Q). Equivalently, kappa_{1/2} factors through the normalizer of the maximal torus T = {t sigma_infinity + u : t^2 + u^2 = det in Z^*} = (Z^[i])^*. This is a non-split Cartan subgroup, the CM torus of the j = 1728 curve; lambda in {1/2, 2, -1} is exactly the harmonic orbit.

Grothendieck first conjectures that kappa_{1/2} is the only such factorization. A margin note corrects this ('Si seulement cela était!'): there is also the case of elliptic curves with extra automorphisms of the other kind.

Case 2 (j = 0), conditions (103)-(104). g = 1, i.e. alpha = f, i.e. xi = f rho(f)^{-1}, i.e. [u, rho] = 1. For arbitrary u one can conjugate by gamma = alpha_0^{-1} (in the extended group pi^~ = pi^ · (1, tau_infinity)) to make u commute with rho. But gamma lies in pi^_{0,3} itself iff epsilon_3(alpha) = 1, iff mu(u) ≡ 1 mod 3 (105).

The next page completes this. The centralizer of rho has index 2 (kernel of the mod-3 cyclotomic sign). Its image in GL(2,Z^) lies in the normalizer of the torus {c rho + d : c^2 - cd + d^2 in Z^*} = (Z^[omega])^*.

What this serves. It is a purely combinatorial (GT-type, 'équation des lacets') analogue of the theorem that the Galois representation on the Tate module of a CM elliptic curve lands in the normalizer of a Cartan subgroup. That theorem is due to Deuring and to Serre's Galois-image work. Here the two CM points with extra automorphisms (j = 1728, j = 0) appear as centralizers of the torsion elements sigma_infinity and rho. The mod-3 condition (105) mirrors the fact that sigma lies in the Cartan itself (not just its normalizer) iff it fixes sqrt(-3), iff chi(sigma) ≡ 1 mod 3.
errors: The first suspicion, that only kappa_{1/2} factors through a normalizer, is false. Grothendieck himself retracts it in the margin: the j = 0 case, worked out immediately below and on the next page, also does.

The margin cites the orbit {1/2, 2, -1} of S_3 together with 'invariant modulaire j=0'. That orbit is the harmonic orbit, j = 1728; the j = 0 points are lambda = -omega, -omega-bar. Either the reading is ambiguous ('1728' seems also written) or this is a slip.
The next page's transcription calls the image a 'Borel normaliseur'. The set {c rho + d} is a torus (a non-split Cartan for Z[omega]), so 'normalisateur du tore' is meant; it cannot be a Borel.
No proof is given that the image is exactly the normalizer rather than a subgroup, or of the uniqueness suspicions. These are left as conjectures.

ideas.what: Centralizer in the loop-equation group of the order-4 elliptic element sigma_infinity maps isomorphically onto the quotient N, giving a section kappa_{1/2} attached to the point lambda = 1/2.
ideas.modern_name: Section/decomposition group at a point with nontrivial automorphisms (orbifold/elliptic points), GT-type section conjecture analogue
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps on GT acting on torsion of profinite PSL_2(Z)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse/Longue Marche discuss M_{1,1} and elliptic points generally; the specific construction is unsure

ideas.what: The image in GL(2,Z^) of the sigma_infinity-centralizer lies in the normalizer of the torus (Z^[i])^*, with tau acting by inversion (99).
ideas.modern_name: Normalizer of non-split Cartan subgroup / CM Galois image at j = 1728
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring, Serre (Galois image for CM curves); combinatorial GT version unsure

ideas.what: j = 0 analogue: [u, rho] = 1; the conjugating element lies in pi^ iff mu(u) ≡ 1 mod 3; the image lies in the normalizer of (Z^[omega])^*.
ideas.modern_name: CM by Z[zeta_3], Cartan versus normalizer distinguished by the mod-3 cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring/Serre for Galois; the combinatorial version is not attributed

ideas.what: Conjecture that these centralizer subgroups are the only subgroups of M^{!~}_{0,3} (or M^!_{0,3}) whose GL_2 image factors through a torus normalizer.
ideas.modern_name: Rigidity/uniqueness of CM-type subgroups in GT-like groups

missed.claim: In the GT-style group of solutions of the loop equation, centralizers of the elliptic elements sigma_infinity (order 4) and rho (order 6) map to GL(2,Z^) through normalizers of the CM tori Z^[i]^* and Z^[omega]^*. This is a combinatorial shadow of Deuring/Serre CM Galois images inside a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type object, including the cyclotomic mod-3 criterion for landing in the Cartan proper.
missed.quote: elle se factorise par le normalisateur du tore maximal T = { t sigma_infty + u ... t^2+u^2 = det(t sigma_infty+u) in Z^* }
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relating GT-type groups and their GL_2(Z^) representations to Cartan normalizers is not standard in the GT literature. It could give a group-theoretic characterization of CM points in anabelian geometry of M_{1,1}.

missed.claim: Uniqueness conjecture: only the centralizers of torsion (CM points with extra automorphisms) give subgroups of M^{!~}_{0,3} whose image factors through a torus normalizer. Grothendieck states it, partially retracts it, and leaves it unproven.
missed.quote: Je suspecte qu'il n'y a que le kappa_{1/2} de (101) ... qui se factorise par un normalisateur
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an anabelian-flavoured rigidity question for GT-type groups acting on profinite SL_2(Z); it appears not to have been formulated in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are elementary, but the page explicitly links the loop-equation (GT-type) group to normalizers of CM Cartan tori at j = 1728 and j = 0, with a uniqueness conjecture. This connection is not, to my knowledge, made in published GT literature, though related elliptic-point work by Ihara, Nakamura and Lochak–Schneps exists.
transcription_corrections: In (105), 'chi(u) = 1 (3)' is better read as 'mu(u) ≡ 1 (3)', consistent with the next page.
'gamma = beta_0^{-1}' is more likely 'gamma = alpha_0^{-1}' (cf. underline{alpha}_0 on the previous page), and in (103) 'beta_0 = 1' is likely 'alpha_0 = 1' (overwritten).
The torus in (102) is likely labelled T_{sigma_infty}, not T_alpha.
'403' over the arrow is likely a page cross-reference, not an arrow label.
The unit group in (102) is Z^* (hat Z), not Lambda^*.
The left margin probably reads 'il y a aussi tous les cas de courbes elliptiques d'invariant modulaire j=...'; the cited orbit {1/2, 2, -1} is the j = 1728 orbit.
